edits.replace_: (Table 7; Figure 14). This is the relaxation time of a head anomaly above the datum — how long a perturbation to the mean water table, such as coastal-retreat or forest-interception drawdown, persists before drainage returns it toward equilibrium. It is not a bound on the seasonal amplitude: summer water-table decline is governed chiefly by evapotranspiration (the β₂ term) and routinely exceeds half the preceding winter rise even where the half-life is long. The half-life describes how quickly a displacement above the datum relaxes back, not how far the water table moves within a season. The eastern open dune turns over rapidly
